Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:10:1.hebrew: אין מורידין קטן לנכסי שבוי - ואפילו הוא ראוי ליורשו, דקא מפסיד להו, ומוטב שיורידו להם איש נכרי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:10:1.english: [The court] does not bring down a minor to the property of a captive - Even if he is fit to inherit him, because he ruins them [the properties], and it is better that they bring down a stranger to them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:10:2.hebrew: ולא קרוב - הראוי לירש בנכסי קטן לעשות ולאכול, כדמסיים טעמיה, דכיון דקטן לא ידע למחויי, אתא האי קרוב לאחזוקי בהן ולומר לחלק ירושתו בא. וטוב להם להוריד איש נכרי, דלא מצי למטען בהו ירושה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:10:2.english: And not a relative - [One] who is fit to inherit [is not installed] into the property of a minor to work [it] and consume [the produce], as [the Gemara] concludes its reason: since a minor does not know how to protest, this relative will come to establish a claim of ownership over [the properties] and say that he came into his share of the inheritance. And it is better for them to install a stranger, who cannot claim inheritance over them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:10:3.hebrew: ולא קרוב מחמת קרוב לנכסי קטן - כגון קטן שיש לו אח מאב, ואותו אח מאב יש לו אח מאם, דאיש נכרי הוא אצל קטן; אין מורידין אותו אח מאם לנכסי קטן מחמת קורבת אחיו של זה, שהוא אח של קטן, דאתי לאחזוקי בהו לצורך אחיו, ויאמר: נכסים הללו של אחי מאמי הם, שנפלו לו מאביו, ואלו לחלקו באו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:10:3.english: And not a relative due to a relative to the property of a minor - For example, a minor who has a paternal brother, and that paternal brother has a maternal brother, who is a stranger to the minor; [the court] does not bring that maternal brother down to the minor's property on account of the kinship of this one's brother, who is the minor's brother, for he might come to take possession of them on behalf of his brother, and say: "These properties belong to my maternal brother, having fallen to him [as an inheritance] from his father, and these came to his portion."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:11:1.hebrew: באחי מאימא - כדפרישית, שזה אח מן האם לאחיו של קטן מן האב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:11:1.english: [In a case of] maternal brothers - As I explained, that this one is a maternal brother to the minor's paternal brother.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:12:1.hebrew: ש"מ מרב הונא - דאמר אין מורידין קרוב לנכסי קטן, שמא יחזיק בהם מחמת ירושה, אבל אחר שאין לו טענת ירושה, מורידין, ולא חיישינן שמא יטעון "אביו של קטן מכרם לי ואכלתים שני חזקה". ש"מ אין מחזיקין בנכסי קטן: אם לא אכל בפני האב שלש שנים, אין שלש שנים שאכלן בפני הקטן חזקה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:12:1.english: Learn from Rav Huna - For he said [that] we do not install a relative into the property of a minor, lest he take possession of it by virtue of inheritance; however, a non-relative, who has no claim of inheritance, we do install, and we are not concerned lest he claim, "The minor's father sold it to me, and I consumed [its produce for the] years of presumptive ownership." Learn from this [that] one cannot establish presumptive ownership of a minor's property: if he did not consume [the produce] in the father's presence for three years, the three years that he consumed it in the minor's presence do not constitute presumptive ownership.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג נטושים על כרחן דכתיב והשביעית תשמטנה ונטשתה - היינו על כרחו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:1:1.english: This is the reading: “Netushim” [means] against their will, as it is written: “And the seventh [year] you shall let it rest and leave it” - That is, against his will.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:1:2.english: Expropriation by the King - The command of the King.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:1:3.hebrew: רטושים מדעתן, דכתיב אם על בנים רוטשה - היינו מדעתו ולא שביה, דכתיב רישיה דקרא: וקם שאון בעמך — היו יראים שלא יבאו אויבים עליהם; וכל מבצריך יושד — יגלו בגולה מאיליהן, וישארו העיירות שדודין מאין איש; כשוד שלמן בית ארבאל ביום מלחמה — כשודדין הבאין למלחמה על ידי מארב על עם היושב בשלום, שלא נזהרו בהם לברוח מפניהם, ושודדים את הכל. וכמוהו (ירמיהו י״ג:י״ט): הגלת יהודה כולה הגלת שלומים — מתוך ישיבת שלום באין מחריד הגלם נבוכדנצר. בית ארבאל — תרגם יהונתן: בית מארב, אל"ף למ"ד יתרים בו, כמו (הושע ב׳:כ״ד) יענו את יזרעאל, שהוא לשון זריעה ולא לשון עיר. ומדקא אמר: יושד כשוד שלמן בית ארבאל, מכלל דההוא יומא לאו בית ארבאל ביום מלחמה הוה, אלא מורך בא בלבם, והמה עוזבים אם על בנים והולכים להם מדאגת האויב, שמא יבא עליהם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:1:3.english: Forsaken of their own volition, as it is written: "A mother was forsaken with her sons" - That is, of his own volition and not [by] captivity, as the beginning of the verse is written: "And a tumult shall arise among your people" — [meaning] they were afraid lest enemies come upon them; "and all your fortresses shall be despoiled" — [meaning] they will go into exile of their own accord, and the cities will remain despoiled, without a man; "as Shalman despoiled Beth-arbel on the day of battle" — like plunderers who come to war by way of ambush against a people dwelling in peace, who were not on guard against them to flee before them, and they plunder everything. And similarly (Jeremiah 13:19): "Judah is exiled, all of it; it is exiled shelomim" — from a peaceful dwelling, with none to frighten [them], Nebuchadnezzar exiled them. "Beth-arbel" [Beit Arbel] — Jonathan translated [it as]: "house of ambush" [beit ma'arav], [the letters] alef [and] lamed being superfluous in it, like (Hosea 2:24) "they shall answer Jezreel [Yizre'el]," which is an expression of sowing and not the name of a city. And since it says: "[all your fortresses] shall be despoiled as Shalman despoiled Beth-arbel," it follows that that day was not [like] Beth-arbel on the day of battle; rather, faintheartedness entered their hearts, and they abandon mother with sons and go away out of anxiety over the enemy, lest he come upon them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:2:1.hebrew: וכולן - מפ' לקמיה אהייא קאי, וכללא לאתויי מאי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:2:1.english: And all of them - [The Gemara] explains further on to which [case] it refers, and what the general rule [comes] to include.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:2:2.hebrew: שמין להם כאריס - אם יבאו הבעלים, יטלו אלו בשבח קרקעות ופירות כמנהג אריסי המקום:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:2:2.english: [They] appraise for them as a sharecropper - If the owners return, these [caretakers] take [a share] of the improvement of the land and the produce, according to the custom of the local sharecroppers.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:2:3.english: Now he is diligent and profits - and he takes everything.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:4:1.hebrew: דאילו התם זריז ונשכר - דכיון ששמעו בו שמת, כי נחת לה, אדעתא דכולהו פירי נחת. אבל הכא דלא שמעו שמת, לאו אדעתא דכולה נחית, אלא ליטול כאריס בכל שנה, ושאר פירות יהא מונחין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:4:1.english: As there, [he is] diligent and profits - For since they heard about him that he died, when he went down to [work] it, he went down with the intention [of taking] all the produce. But here, where they did not hear that he died, he did not go down with the intention [of taking] all of it, rather to take [a share] like a sharecropper each year, and the rest of the produce shall remain [deposited].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:5:1.english: His wife's property - Melog property, where he consumes the produce and the principal is hers.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:5:2.english: He spent much and consumed little produce - before he died or divorced her.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:1.hebrew: הא לא דמיא - תרוצא הוא. הא דנכסי שבויין להא דאשתו קטנה דמי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:1.english: This is comparable only - This is an answer: this [case] of the property of captives is comparable to that [case] of his minor wife.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:2.hebrew: קטנה - שהיא יתומה שהשיאוה אמה ואחיה, ואין קידושין תופסין בה מן התורה אלא מדברי סופרים. לפיכך, יוצאה במיאון בע"כ אם תמאן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:2.english: [His] minor [wife] - Who is an orphan whose mother and brothers married her off, and betrothal does not take effect upon her by Torah law, only by rabbinic decree. Therefore, she leaves [the marriage] through refusal against his will if she refuses.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:3.hebrew: כמוציא על נכסי אחר דמי - ואם הוציא ולא אכל כדי הוצאתו, שמין לו כאריס:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:3.english: [He] is like one who outlays [expenditures] on the property of another - And if he outlaid [expenditures] and did not consume [produce] equal to his expenditure, they assess [it] for him like a sharecropper.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:4.hebrew: דלא סמכא דעתיה - שיהא מוחזק בידו, דדואג שמא תמאן בו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:4.english: That he does not rely [on it] - that it will be securely in his possession, for he is worried lest she refuse him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:5.english: The Sages instituted for him - To take [a share] like a sharecropper.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:6.hebrew: כי היכי דלא ניפסדינהו - שלא יקלקל הקרקעות לזורען תמיד, ולא יעבוד ולא יעדור כרמים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:6:6.english: So that he will not ruin them - That he should not ruin the lands by sowing them constantly, and not tilling or hoeing vineyards.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:8:1.english: To include that of Rav Nachman - One who flees due to murder [meradin].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:8:2.hebrew: יצא לדעת אין מורידין - דכיון שהיה שפוי בדעתו ולא צוהו בלכתו לירד לנכסיו, ש"מ לא ניחא ליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:8:2.english: [If] he left of [his own] volition, [we] do not authorize [a relative] to descend - For since he was of sound mind and did not instruct him upon leaving to descend to his property, learn from this [that] he is not pleased [with it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:8:3.english: One who flees is like a captive - For his mind is not settled because he is panicked.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:8:4.english: Due to a tax [karga] - Because he has nothing with which to pay his head tax to the king, and he flees before the time [for payment] arrives.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:8:5.english: That is [one who] leaves of [his own] volition - For there is no panic here.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:8:6.hebrew: מחמת מרדין - שהרג את הנפש, ופרסאי הורגין על שפיכות דמים, כדאמרינן בבבא קמא (דף קיז.). מרדין היא רציחה בלשון פרסי, וכן מפורש בשערים דרב האי גאון (שער מ):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:8:6.english: Due to meradin - [Meaning] that he killed a person, and the Persians execute for bloodshed, as we say in Bava Kamma (117a). Meradin is murder in the Persian language, and so is it explained in She'arim of Rav Hai Gaon (Gate 40).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:9:1.hebrew: מעמידין אפוטרופוס - להכניס דבר המוכן ויהא שמור לבעלים, ואח"כ מורידין קרוב להשביח וליטול כאריס:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:9:1.english: They appoint a steward - To bring in that which is ready, and it will be preserved for the owner; and afterward they bring down a relative [to the property] to improve [it] and to take [a share] like a sharecropper.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:9:2.english: And let [the court] appoint a steward forever - So that he will not take anything.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:9:3.hebrew: אפוטרופא לדיקנני לא מוקמינן - אין בית דין טורחין לבקש אפוטרופוס לאנשים גדולים שנתמלא זקנם, לפי שלא ימצאוהו. דבשלמא ליתמי, איכא דשמע להו והוי אפוטרופוס לדבר מצוה, אבל לדיקנני לא שמעי להו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 39a:9:3.english: We do not appoint a steward for the bearded - The court does not trouble itself to seek a steward for grown men whose beards have filled out, because they will not find one. For while for orphans there is [someone] who will heed them and become a steward for a mitzvah, for the bearded [adults] they will not heed them.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 39a:12:1.hebrew: ש"מ מדרב הונא אין מחזיקין בנכסי קטן ואפי' הגדיל - פרש"י: מדאמר רב הונא "אין מורידין קרוב", הא נכרי מורידין. וקשה: דבלא רב הונא כמה משניות יש שמעמידין אפוטרופוס לנכסי יתומים, פרק הניזקין (גיטין דף נב.): "מנהו ב"ד לא ישבע". וע"ק: היכי מוכח מדרב הונא דאין מחזיקין? דלמא אי טוען שני חזקה — מועיל, והא דמורידין נכרי, משום דליכא למיחש למידי; דע"כ כיון דמורידין, א"כ יש לו דעת לומר: "הבא עדים שלקחת מאבי", והכי נמי יש לו לדעת ולמחות בסוף כל שלשה. וכי תימא: הא פשיטא ליה דאינו יודע למחות בסוף ג', אף ע"פ שהוא נזכר לשאול עידי מכירה, דרגילות הוא טפי לשכוח מחאה בסוף כל ג' — א"כ בלא רב הונא פשיטא דאין מחזיקין. וי"ל: דאי לאו רב הונא, ממה שמעמידין אפוטרופוס לנכסי יתומין אין להוכיח דאין מחזיקין; דאפילו מחזיקין, לא חיישינן שמא יחזיק, דב"ד לא יבררו כי אם נאמן, או משום דידע למחות בסוף כל ג' כדפרישית. אבל מדאמר רב הונא "אין מורידין קרוב", א"כ חושש לרמאות, וגם אית ליה דלא ידע למחות בקרוב ולומר "שדה זו של אבי ולא הגיע לחלקך" — אם כן בנכרי נמי לא ידע למחות, ולכך אין מחזיקין. וא"ת: כמו שיש לו לדעת ולומר לנכרי לשאול עידי מכירה, כמו כן יהיה לו דעת לומר לקרובו "אייתי ראיה שזה הגיע לחלקך"? וי"ל: דגבי קרוב, סבור שאומר אמת, שהרי של אביהם היה השדה, ולא אסיק אדעתיה לומר "אייתי ראייה"; אבל לנכרי מסיק אדעתיה למימר "אייתי ראייה עידי מכירה":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 39a:12:1.english: "Learn from Rav Huna['s statement] that one cannot assume presumptive ownership of the property of a minor," and even [after] he has grown up - Rashi explained: Since Rav Huna said, "We do not place a relative [in possession]," [this implies that] a non-relative we do place [in possession]. And this is difficult, for even without Rav Huna, there are several Mishnayot [stating] that we appoint a guardian for the property of orphans, [such as in] the chapter [entitled] HaNizakin (Gittin 52a): "If the court appointed him, he need not take an oath." And there is a further difficulty: How is it proven from Rav Huna that one cannot assume presumptive ownership? Perhaps if he claims [to have held it for] the years of presumptive ownership, it is effective, and the reason we place a non-relative [in possession] is because there is nothing to be concerned about — for perforce, since we place [him in possession], it must be that [the orphan, upon growing up,] has the presence of mind to say, "Bring witnesses that you bought [it] from my father," and likewise he has the presence of mind to protest at the end of every three [years]. And if you will say: It is obvious to him that he does not know to protest at the end of three [years] even though he remembers to ask for witnesses of purchase, since it is more common to forget [to make] a protest at the end of every three [years] — if so, even without Rav Huna it would be obvious that one cannot assume presumptive ownership. And one can answer: Were it not for Rav Huna, from [the fact] that we appoint a guardian for the property of orphans one could not prove that one cannot assume presumptive ownership; for even if one could assume presumptive ownership, we would not be concerned lest he seize [the property], because the court will choose only a trustworthy person, or because [the orphan] knows to protest at the end of every three [years], as I have explained. However, since Rav Huna said, "We do not place a relative [in possession]," it follows that he is concerned about deceit, and he also holds that [the orphan] would not know to protest against a relative and say, "This field belonged to my father and did not fall to your share." If so, against a non-relative as well he would not know to protest, and therefore one cannot assume presumptive ownership. And if you will say: Just as he has the presence of mind to speak to a non-relative [and] ask for witnesses of purchase, so too he should have the presence of mind to say to his relative, "Bring proof that this fell to your share"? One can answer: Regarding a relative, he assumes that [the relative] is telling the truth, since the field indeed belonged to their father, and it does not occur to him to say, "Bring proof"; whereas to a non-relative, it does occur to him to say, "Bring proof — witnesses of purchase."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 39a:2:1.hebrew: וכולם שמין להם כאריס - אנטושים דרשב"ג קאי, כדמסיק. פי' רש"י: דבשבוי ששמע שמתו — אוכל כל הפירות, ואם יבואו הבעלים קודם שיאכל הפירות, יטול כשאר אריסין ויחזיר השאר; ובנטושים, דלא שמע שמת — לא יאכל כל הפירות, אלא שמין הפירות שיאכל כשאר אריסין, למחצה, לשליש ולרביע, ולא יאכל כלום בחנם. וקשה: דאמאי משני לעיל "לירד ולמכור תנן"? לישני "לירד ולאכול תנן", דהא אפילו לאכול בחנם אינו יורד! ועוד: מאי פריך בתר הכי "אף בניהם כלל לא"? הא ודאי אין לו כלל, אפילו למ"ד מורידין, כיון שאין לו אלא כאריס נכרי. ועוד: מאי פריך מהמוציא הוצאות על נכסי אשתו? דהתם יורד לאכול כל הפירות, אבל הכא אינו יורד כי אם בתורת אריסות. ותו: דאמר שמואל לקמן: "שבוי שהניח קמה לקצור — מעמידין אפוטרופוס וקוצר ובוצר, ואח"כ מורידין קרוב לנכסיו"; ומעיקרא אמאי אין מורידין קרוב, כיון שלא יאכל הפירות בחנם? לכך נראה דודאי שכל הפירות אוכל בחנם, ואם זבל וחרש וזרע, ובעלים באו קודם שקצר — יטול כאריס שכר טרחו ועמלו. ולרב, וכן לת"ק, אית להו שאין שמין כאריס, ולכך אין מורידין דלמא מפסיד להו; לפי שירא שיבואו הבעלים קודם שיקצור ויאכל ולא יטול כלום, ולא ישביח הקרקע, אלא כל מה שימצא יאכל בחנם, כדין קרוב היורד לנכסי שבוי. והשתא פריך שפיר: כיון שאוכל כל הפירות, כשיבואו הבעלים קודם שילקט אמאי נוטל כאריס, טפי מהמוציא הוצאות על נכסי אשתו כו'? והא דקאמר "ואילו התם זריז ונשכר", פי': כששמע הבעלים ממשמשים ובאין, מניחין אותו לקדם ולתלוש, אע"פ שהפירות ישוו הרבה מעמלו, כיון שאם לא יקדם אין משלמין טרחו; אבל הכא בנטושים, אם באו בעלים, אין מניחין אותו לתלוש, כיון דלא מפסיד מידי, דשיימי' להו כאריס:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 39a:2:1.english: And [for] all of them, [the court] appraises their [work] as [that of] a sharecropper - This refers to abandoned [property] (netushim) according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, as [the Gemara] concludes. Rashi explained: in the case of a captive regarding whom [people] heard that he died, [the relative] eats all the produce, and if the owners come before he eats the produce, he takes like other sharecroppers and returns the rest; whereas in the case of abandoned [property], where he did not hear that [the owner] died, he does not eat all the produce, rather they appraise the produce so that he eats like other sharecroppers — a half, a third, or a quarter — and he eats nothing for free. And this is difficult: why did [the Gemara] answer earlier, "We learned [the Mishnah regarding] descending to sell"? Let it answer, "We learned [regarding] descending to eat," for he does not even descend to eat for free! And furthermore, why does [the Gemara] ask after this, "[Does it mean] even their children [have] nothing at all?" Surely he has nothing at all, even according to the one who says we install [a relative], since he only has [the rights] of an ordinary sharecropper! And furthermore, why does it ask from "one who outlays expenditures on his wife's property"? For there he descends to eat all the produce, whereas here he descends only under the status of sharecropping! And furthermore, Shmuel says below: "[In the case of] a captive who left standing grain to reap, we appoint a guardian, and he reaps and harvests [the grapes], and afterward we install a relative into his property"; yet initially, why do we not install a relative, since he will not eat the produce for free? Therefore, it appears that certainly he eats all the produce for free, and if he fertilized, plowed, and sowed, and the owners came before he reaped, he takes like a sharecropper as compensation for his toil and labor. And Rav, and likewise the first tanna, hold that we do not appraise [his work] like a sharecropper, and therefore we do not install [a relative] lest he cause them loss — for he fears that the owners might come before he reaps and eats, and he will take nothing; [thus] he will not improve the land, rather whatever he finds he will eat for free, like the law of a relative who descends into the property of a captive. And now [the Gemara] asks well: since he eats all the produce, when the owners come before he gathers [it], why does he take like a sharecropper, more than "one who outlays expenditures on his wife's property," etc.? And as for what [the Gemara] says, "Whereas there, he is diligent and profits," the meaning is: when he heard that the owners are drawing near and coming, they allow him to go ahead and pluck [the produce], even though the produce is worth much more than his labor, since if he does not go ahead they do not pay [for] his toil; whereas here with abandoned [property], if the owners came, they do not allow him to pluck [it], since he loses nothing, as we appraise [their work] for them like a sharecropper:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 39a:8:1.hebrew: אמר שמואל שבוי שנשבה מורידין - וא"ת: והאמרה שמואל חדא זימנא? וי"ל דה"ק: אף על גב דבשבוי מורידין, יצא לדעת — אין מורידין:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 39a:8:1.english: Shmuel said: [For] a captive who was taken captive, [the court] authorizes [a relative] to descend - And if you ask: Didn't Shmuel say it once [already]? One can answer that this is what he is saying: Even though for a captive [the court] authorizes [a relative] to descend, [if] he left of [his own] volition, [the court] does not authorize [a relative] to descend:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 39a:8:2.hebrew: היינו לדעת - דמסתמא לא פליג אשמואל, מדלא קאמר "אף בורח" או "אף יוצא לדעת":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 39a:8:2.english: That is [the case of one who left] of [his own] volition - For presumably [Rav Naḥman] does not disagree with Shmuel, since he did not say "even one who flees" or "even one who leaves of his own volition."
